pages.text: "Finished! I am going!" Kiki, the pointy-eared cat, dropped the snow shovel. The bucket stayed in the middle of the alley too.
"Tomorrow, I will build a snow-brick wall with these!" Kiki told Nono, the smallest, roundest sparrow. Nono nodded. Snow fell softly.
Next morning, the whole alley was white. No shovel or bucket in sight. "Where is my shovel?"
Kiki dug and dug. Nothing! A toe struck something hard. "Ow! What is that?" It was the buried bucket.
Kiki's ears drooped. A wall to build, but no shovel. "I do not know where it is..."
Grandpa pointed to the shop wall. A broom and sled leaned side by side. No snow had piled on them.
"Leave things out, and snow covers them. Put them against the wall." Grandpa tapped an empty space. "Against the wall—there!" Kiki repeated.
Gugu and Nono came to help clear the snow. Out came the shovel! Against the wall went the shovel, then the bucket beside it.
At evening, Kiki raised the shovel. "One, gather your things after playing! Two, to the shop wall! Three, side by side!" Snow fell again.

Next morning, the shovel was still there. Nono held Kiki's hand. Put things away, and you can play right away tomorrow. Kiki touched the green bell and built the snow-brick wall. "Against the wall—there!"
